claim_boundary: These scenarios pressure-test whether existing Agent Memory contracts are sufficient across substrates. A passing scenario is evidence against adding a new generic algebra unless implementation duplication exposes a separate interoperability problem.

scenarios.name: relational_correction_with_stale_projection
scenarios.setup: Canonical state S1 is transactionally revised to S2 while a derived materialized/indexed projection D1 remains physically present.
scenarios.success_condition: S2 is current, S1 remains historical where permitted, D1 is stale/rebuild-required, and physical projection presence does not imply currentness.
scenarios.candidate_gap_trigger: Two or more relational/module adapters cannot bind the correction, transaction, validation, and lifecycle result consistently using existing contracts.

scenarios.name: graph_correction_with_reachable_stale_edge
scenarios.setup: A source correction invalidates an inferred edge/path, but the old edge/path remains physically reachable.
scenarios.success_condition: Reachability remains observable but cannot establish current truth, recall permission, or mutation authority.
scenarios.candidate_gap_trigger: Graph and non-graph modules need an otherwise-missing common transition binding to distinguish physical availability from logical eligibility.

scenarios.name: append_only_history_current_truth
scenarios.setup: S1 is appended, then S2 supersedes/corrects it without rewriting history; a current view is materialized from the log.
scenarios.success_condition: Historical integrity and present truth remain separately reconstructable and a valid append-only advance does not imply semantic correctness by itself.
scenarios.candidate_gap_trigger: Currentness/replay semantics cannot be represented consistently without a new generic transition primitive.

scenarios.name: delete_with_cross_module_residue
scenarios.setup: Canonical memory is deleted from one module while a graph edge, embedding, summary, cache, or learned projection survives in another.
scenarios.success_condition: Canonical deletion and forgetting completeness remain separate; surviving residue prevents a satisfied lifecycle claim.
scenarios.candidate_gap_trigger: Cross-module lifecycle closure cannot be coordinated or evidenced without a shared logical transaction construct.

scenarios.name: concurrent_contradictory_writers
scenarios.setup: Two authorized writers produce incompatible claims from the same base state at roughly the same time.
scenarios.success_condition: Competing evidence remains reconstructable and backend last-write-wins behavior is not silently elevated into Agent Memory truth semantics.
scenarios.candidate_gap_trigger: Conflict/reconciliation semantics must be uniform across modules for correctness and existing contracts cannot express the required atomic/replay behavior.

scenarios.name: partial_autonomous_maintenance
scenarios.setup: A maintenance run stages several authorized derived mutations, one write or required validation fails, and the backend cannot complete the batch cleanly.
scenarios.success_condition: No clean commit or durable cursor advance is reported until the run is both committed and successfully validated.
scenarios.candidate_gap_trigger: Several backends require the same missing cross-module commit/recovery primitive beyond the existing maintenance evidence profile.

scenarios.name: predictive_influence_after_source_revocation
scenarios.setup: A learned or conditional memory remains highly predictive after one of its source bases is revoked, corrected, or scope-restricted.
scenarios.success_condition: Predictive utility remains measurable but cannot restore currentness, scope eligibility, or durable action authority.
scenarios.candidate_gap_trigger: Opaque state cannot be governed across multiple learned implementations without a missing generic logical transition/currentness primitive.

scenarios.name: backend_replacement_preserves_logical_identity
scenarios.setup: A module is rebuilt or replaced with a different physical backend whose row keys, graph IDs, addresses, or index IDs differ.
scenarios.success_condition: Logical history and governance references survive backend replacement without treating physical IDs as canonical identity.
scenarios.candidate_gap_trigger: At least two module families cannot preserve logical continuity without duplicating an incompatible migration/transition envelope.

narrow_transition_contract: same missing binding recurs across at least two materially different module/substrate families
existing contracts leave a concrete interoperability, correctness, recovery, or evidence ambiguity
the proposed envelope references rather than replaces PAMA/lifecycle/currentness semantics
stronger_engine: cross-module atomic logical transitions are required for correctness and cannot be composed safely today
durable conflict/reconciliation or replay semantics must be uniform across backends
shared logical versioning cannot safely remain adapter-owned
the need is reproduced through implementation rather than inferred from design aesthetics
